stress.title: Stress
stress.description: Stress is the body's response to pressure or demands that feel hard to manage.
coping: Break the biggest task into one small step.
Take a 5-minute break away from screens.
Write down what is in your control and what is not.
stress.seek_help: If stress stays high for weeks or affects daily life, a counsellor can help.
stress.safety_note: Stress is common and is not a personal failing.

anxiety.title: Anxiety
anxiety.description: Anxiety is a feeling of worry or fear that can show up in both thoughts and body.
coping: Try slowly breathing in for 4 and out for 6.
Name 3 things you can see around you.
Write the worry down, then note one small action.
anxiety.seek_help: If worry feels constant or stops you doing things, consider talking to a professional.
anxiety.safety_note: Anxious feelings are uncomfortable but usually pass.

low_mood.title: Low mood
low_mood.description: Low mood is a lasting feeling of sadness, emptiness or loss of interest.
coping: Try one small activity you used to enjoy.
Step outside for a short walk or some daylight.
Reach out to one person today, even briefly.
low_mood.seek_help: If low mood lasts more than two weeks, please speak to a doctor or counsellor.
low_mood.safety_note: Ask for help early; you do not need to wait until it is severe.

loneliness.title: Loneliness
loneliness.description: Loneliness is the pain of feeling disconnected from others, even around people.
coping: Send a short message to someone you trust.
Join one small group or activity, online or offline.
Spend a few minutes somewhere with other people around.
loneliness.seek_help: If loneliness feels heavy for a long time, a counsellor or support group can help.
loneliness.safety_note: Many people feel this way; reaching out is a strength.

sleep_problems.title: Sleep problems
sleep_problems.description: Sleep difficulties include trouble falling asleep, waking often or sleeping too little.
coping: Keep a regular bedtime and wake time.
Avoid screens for 30 minutes before bed.
If awake for a long time, get up and do something calm.
sleep_problems.seek_help: If sleep problems last several weeks, talk to a doctor.
sleep_problems.safety_note: This tool does not advise on sleep medication.

academic_stress.title: Academic stress
academic_stress.description: Pressure from exams, grades, deadlines or expectations about studies.
coping: Make a simple study plan with short blocks and breaks.
Start with the smallest topic to build momentum.
Talk to a teacher or friend about what is unclear.
academic_stress.seek_help: If study pressure affects sleep or health, talk to a college counsellor.
academic_stress.safety_note: Grades do not define your worth.

work_stress.title: Work stress
work_stress.description: Strain from workload, deadlines, conflict or job insecurity.
coping: Pick your top three priorities for tomorrow.
Take short breaks during the day.
Try to set a clear end to your work day.
work_stress.seek_help: If work stress is affecting health, consider talking to a professional or your workplace support service.
work_stress.safety_note: Your wellbeing matters more than any single task.

burnout.title: Burnout
burnout.description: Burnout is deep exhaustion from long-term stress, often with cynicism and low drive.
coping: Protect one small block of rest each day.
Say no to one non-essential demand this week.
Talk to someone about your workload.
burnout.seek_help: Persistent exhaustion deserves a check-in with a doctor or counsellor.

overthinking.title: Overthinking
overthinking.description: Overthinking is repeating the same thoughts or worries without reaching a solution.
coping: Set a 10-minute worry time, then move on.
Try grounding by naming 5 things you can see.
Ask what is one thing you can do about this today.
overthinking.seek_help: If thoughts feel uncontrollable, a counsellor can teach helpful strategies.

anger.title: Anger
anger.description: Anger is a natural emotion that often sits on top of hurt, stress or feeling unheard.
coping: Pause and take a few slow breaths before responding.
Step away for a short walk to cool down.
Name what may be underneath the anger, like hurt or stress.
anger.seek_help: If anger often leads to regret or conflict, consider talking to a counsellor.
anger.safety_note: If you feel you might hurt someone, step away and contact emergency support.

social_isolation.title: Social isolation
social_isolation.description: Social isolation is spending much less time with others than you would like or need.
coping: Plan one small, low-pressure social moment.
Reply to one message you have been putting off.
Tell someone you trust that you have been withdrawing.
social_isolation.seek_help: If you keep avoiding people for weeks, consider speaking to a professional.

healthy_coping.title: Healthy coping
healthy_coping.description: Simple habits that support emotional wellbeing.
coping: Move your body for 10 minutes.
Keep regular meals and sleep.
Spend a little time on something you enjoy.
healthy_coping.seek_help: Self-care helps, but it does not replace professional support when you need it.

breathing_exercises.title: Breathing exercises
breathing_exercises.description: Slow breathing can calm the body's stress response.
coping: Breathe in for 4 counts and out for 6, five times.
Rest a hand on your belly and breathe slowly into it.
Try box breathing with 4 counts each for in, hold, out and hold.
breathing_exercises.seek_help: If breathing exercises make you dizzy, stop and breathe normally.

grounding_techniques.title: Grounding techniques
grounding_techniques.description: Grounding brings attention back to the present moment.
coping: Try 5-4-3-2-1 grounding by naming 5 things you see, 4 you feel, 3 you hear, 2 you smell and 1 you taste.
Press your feet into the floor and notice the sensation.
Describe your surroundings out loud in detail.
grounding_techniques.seek_help: If distress stays intense, reach out to someone you trust.

when_to_seek_help.title: When to seek professional help
when_to_seek_help.description: Professional support helps when distress is persistent or affects daily life.
common_signs: trouble at school, work or in relationships
coping: Consider talking to a counsellor, doctor or therapist.
Tell someone you trust that you are struggling.
Ask your college or workplace about support services.
when_to_seek_help.seek_help: If you ever feel unsafe, contact emergency services right away.
when_to_seek_help.safety_note: Asking for help is a sign of strength.

emergency_support.title: Emergency support
emergency_support.description: Steps to take if you or someone else may be in immediate danger.
coping: Contact your local emergency service or a crisis line now.
Go to the nearest emergency department.
Stay with someone you trust and tell them how you feel.
emergency_support.seek_help: Do not wait; urgent support is available.
emergency_support.safety_note: Emergency numbers differ by country and are set in the app configuration.

case_stress.title: Worry about the case or court
case_stress.description: Waiting for hearings, repeating your story and facing the legal process can feel exhausting and frightening.
common_signs: feeling helpless about what will happen
coping: Ask your lawyer or support person to explain the next step in simple words.
Write your questions on a paper and keep it with you on the day of the hearing.
Plan for someone you trust to sit with you on the day of the hearing.
Take a few slow breaths before you enter the room, and drink some water.
case_stress.seek_help: A counsellor or victim-support officer can walk with you through the process.
case_stress.safety_note: You are not alone in this process.

fear_safety.title: Fear and feeling unsafe
fear_safety.description: Fear can stay in the body for a long time after a frightening experience.
common_signs: checking doors or phone again and again
coping: Think of one place where you feel a little safer, and spend some time there.
Keep the number of one trusted person ready on your phone.
Press your feet on the floor and name five things you can see around you.
Tell one trusted person that you are feeling unsafe, so you are not carrying it alone.
fear_safety.seek_help: If you feel unsafe right now, please contact the local emergency number or someone nearby.

shame_guilt.title: Guilt or shame
shame_guilt.description: Many people blame themselves for things that were never in their control.
coping: Speak to yourself the way you would speak to a dear friend in the same situation.
Share this feeling with one person who will not judge you.
Write down the thought, and then write what you would tell a friend who had the same thought.
shame_guilt.seek_help: A counsellor can help you carry this feeling in a lighter way.
shame_guilt.safety_note: Feeling guilty does not mean you did something wrong.

upsetting_memories.title: Upsetting memories
upsetting_memories.description: Painful memories can come back suddenly, even when you try to push them away.
common_signs: feeling as if it is happening again
coping: When a memory comes, look around and name five things you can see right now.
Put your hand on your chest and breathe slowly until the feeling passes.
Remind yourself that this is a memory and it is not happening now.
Splash some cool water on your face or hold a warm cup of chai in both hands.
upsetting_memories.seek_help: If memories keep disturbing your sleep or day, a trained counsellor can help.
upsetting_memories.safety_note: These reactions are common and they can ease with support.
